findings.quote: It is confirmed: escape always costs the bacterium something.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind_pick C). A ("escape always costs") and D ("none of the mutants turned out to be weakened at all") are mirrored absolutes that a form-only reader discards on sight, halving the item to B vs C before the passage is opened. C is then the hedged middle. Not decided blind (B is a live alternative), so flag rather than kill.

findings.quote: Interested, but unwilling to let the results so far settle the question.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE / genre convention (blind_pick B). In science-journalism prose the writer's stance is almost always the cautious middle, and B is the only qualified stance among three strong ones (Dismissive / Persuaded / Detached). Distractors are substantive positions and the passage would ground the answer, so flag, not kill - but a test-wise student can pick B without reading.

findings.quote: That they all fell in the eight weeks following a tamping machine's visit.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind_pick B). C logically entails B ("two thirds of them came soon after a tamping machine had been through"): if all buckles fell within eight weeks of tamping, then two thirds came soon after tamping. Under a single-key convention the stronger option cannot be the unique answer, so a reader with zero domain knowledge eliminates C by pure logic and is left leaning to the surviving quantified sibling. Still 3-way undecided against A and D, so flag, not kill.

findings.quote: Att färgen gick ända in till mitten.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind_pick C). The cut test - slicing the hide and checking that the tan has penetrated to the core - is the standard craft criterion for a finished vegetable-tanned hide, so anyone who knows tanning picks C blind. The other three (elapsed time, spent liquor, target weight) are substantively plausible craft criteria and the passage would genuinely ground the choice, so flag rather than kill.

findings.quote: Skomakarna gick över till fabrikernas ovandelar när garveriet lade ned kalvlinjen.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind_pick A). D is circular as an answer to "skälet till att kalvskinnen försvann": it makes the tannery's closing of the calf line the cause of the shoemakers' switch, i.e. it presupposes the very disappearance it is asked to explain - visible from stem form alone. B ("All efterfrågan ... hade upphört") is an absolute a form-only reader also discards. Two eliminations leave A vs C at even odds, materially better than chance.

findings.quote: Ungefär var femte bokad timme saknade redovisad verksamhet, mest bland de pass som gått i arv.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind_pick D). Two form-only eliminations: B is an absolute ("Samtliga föreningar ... minst en bokad timme oanvänd varje vecka") and C is self-undermining (a review whose headline finding is that its own data cannot be used). That leaves A vs D, which are opposites, and D is the quantified/hedged sibling. Cross-question corroboration compounds it: q:2 option B ("Att den inte behövs om tiderna omprövas årligen") presupposes that the wasted hours sit in slots that are NOT re-examined each term, which is exactly D and the negation of A - so the sheet's own second question tips the first.

findings.quote: Namnsdagsfirandet upphörde helt och hållet i samma stund som hushållen slutade slå upp almanackan.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind_pick B). A pairs two extreme absolutes ("helt och hållet", "i samma stund") and is discarded on form; C and D each lean on a superlative ("viktigaste råd", "framför allt"), while B is the only two-clause qualified statement. On a "överensstämmer bäst" stem the hedged option is the test-wise pick, so the item runs materially better than chance blind. Not decided by form alone (C and D remain substantive readings), hence flag.

findings.quote: bör inte överstiga vad mottagaren utan besvär kan ge igen
findings.note: class 6: 'ge igen' in modern Swedish overwhelmingly reads as 'retaliate / get even' (ge igen för ngt, ge igen med samma mynt); the intended sense here is reciprocation of a gift, which lands as an unintended double meaning inside a quoted etiquette rule. Native alternative: 'kan gengälda' or 'kan ge tillbaka'. Taste-level only, and partly defensible as 1934 period usage in a quoted source, so recorded as minor rather than a conviction.
